catalog_quote: [Batic 2019: 67, Table 1] Syllabic structure — Moderately complex: CV, CVV, CVC, and rarely CVVC. | Tonal system — Simple: two-way contrast. Tone levelling towards low tones has been observed (cf. Tangale, Piya and Widala, LEGER 2014: 233). ... [Batic 2019: 68, §2] Kushi verbs are either monosyllabic or disyllabic. For operational reasons, the citation form used throughout this paper is the imperative form. ... [Batic 2017 wordlist: 85] Kushi has two contrastive tones, high (H) and low (L), and two contour tones, falling (HL) and rasing (LH). Tones are always marked. If the vowel is long, the tone is marked only on the first vowel (e.g. ɓɔ̀ɔlì ‘North’). ... [Batic 2017 story: <12>] Kushi is a tonal language distinguishing between two punctual tones – high and low. In the text presented below low tones are marked with a grave accent, while discrete high tones are left unmarked. High tones are marked only in contour tones (ex. tóò ‘well’). Vowel length is also indicated, with the tone marked on the first vowel (ex. pèemò ‘he’).
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kushi is described as a two-tone (H/L, plus HL and LH contours) language with a tendency to level tones toward low; none of the accessible first-hand descriptions (all by Batic, plus Leger's areal papers) says anything about word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; only the areal remark that tone is being levelled toward a 'frozen' low tone in the southern Bole-Tangale languages (Leger 2014: 230-234, not seen).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone marked on every syllable in citation forms (imperative for verbs); no word- or phrase-level stress domain discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Kushi = Goji (fɔ̀k Gòjì), kush1236/kuh, Kushi village area, Shongom LGA, Gombe State; Batic notes an east (Gomle, Dirang; conservative) vs west (Kauri, Kommo) Kushi internal split but his data are not dialect-restricted. Not to be confused with Pero (pero1241), listed by Glottolog among Kushi's alternate names.
